mechanism.base: The hard overcomes the soft, the old texts say, and so metal has its way with wood. Left alone a tree grows every direction, tall and loose and full of shoots that lead nowhere. The knife gives it a shape. It takes the branch that crowds the crown, lets light in and squares the timber for a beam. Nothing in the grain asks for the edge, and all the tree becomes passes through it.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Metal, the tree grows every way at once and nothing prunes it into a shape. Height comes without a finish. Take on one rule you did not write and keep it.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Metal, the knife outruns the tree and every new shoot meets the edge. Nothing stands long enough to bear. Let one thing grow a season before anyone judges it.

function.definition_catalyst: Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Metal makes it hard and exact, the finish growth needs. As a catalyst, the line runs faint. Most of your order is the order you bring, and little of it comes handed down.
function.definition_friction: Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Metal turns it exact, a line over your growth. As a friction, the line turns inward, because order is where you feel safe. The bar rises each time you clear it, and enough never comes.
function.definition_balanced: Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Metal makes it hard and exact, the finish growth needs. In balance, the line holds firm without closing in. You keep the standards you chose and still leave space to grow.
function.advise_catalyst: Little of the order in your life comes from outside you. Join one class that meets at a set time. Clear out one drawer and keep only what you use. Follow one training plan set by someone else for a whole month.
function.advise_friction: Seek Water, the Mind energy. Water feeds the tree from below, and growth returns faster than the knife takes it. Let it heal what Metal cuts. You answer to more rules than anyone has set you. Give one evening a week to learning something nobody grades. Take one whole day this month with no plan and no messages.
function.advise_balanced: Your line holds firm and still bends where your growth needs it to. Clear out one drawer and keep only what you use. Choose one rule you keep and test this month whether it still serves you.

candidates.cta_verdict: You grow best with a line to grow against, and you finish more under someone else's rule than under your own plan.

catalyst.clause: the tree grows every way at once and nothing prunes it into a shape
catalyst.remedy: Take on one rule you did not write and keep it.

friction.clause: the knife outruns the tree and every new shoot meets the edge
friction.remedy: Let one thing grow a season before anyone judges it.

wide.clause: There is no shortage of Metal in you, the knife a growing tree needs to take its shape.
wide.remedy: Use it. Finish one thing to the line this month.

missing.clause: No knife near the tree, so growth goes wherever it likes and nothing gets finished.
missing.remedy: Borrow a rule, a deadline or someone above you.

spared.clause: No knife at the tree, and the tree is better for it, free to take its own shape.
spared.remedy: Keep it so. Set your own rules and keep them.

thin.clause: A small knife at a big tree, enough to shape it and never enough to cut it back.
thin.remedy: Keep it small. One rule, kept, is plenty.

excess.clause: Too much knife at a young tree, and the trunk is cut through before it can stand.
excess.remedy: Put the knife down. Rest, read, let the trunk regrow.

mechanism_yin.base: The hard prevails over the soft, and so metal comes for wood: the shears meet the hedge, the pruning knife meets the vine, and wild growth learns the shape it could not find alone. Unpruned, a vine sprawls and fruits little. Under the edge it loses tendrils and gains a harvest.
mechanism_yin.friction_turn: Run heavy, the cutting never stops: cut after cut until growing feels like a fault. Too much knife leaves no vine. Step back from blades that prune for pruning's sake.

__ore.retired_fn_body: The Duty is your accountability function: how order, obligation, and other people’s standards sit on you. With Metal running it, accountability in you is exact: contracts, deadlines, people who measure. You grow best trellised, and you know it, which is why you keep choosing exacting company. Respect the shears that shape you, and refuse the ones that only wound.
__ore.retired_base_personal: Your core is Wood, and Metal tames Wood: the knife prunes the branch. Metal is the edge that comes for your growth, rules, reviews, hard standards, and pruning is precisely what turns wild reach into an orchard. That is why Metal is your Order, the discipline that shapes you. Unpruned trees grow large. Pruned ones bear fruit.

backlog_dips_tg_pattern.action: A hard rule concentrates you: given clean constraints, your growth goes vertical.

__ore.retired_v3_definition_catalyst:
Metal is your Order, and as a catalyst, it is the standard that shapes your growth: editors, coaches, reviews, rules you chose on purpose. You improve fastest under exacting eyes.

Coachable, honest about your own work, better every year that someone demanding stays close. The teacher who marked hard, the friend who says the draft is not there yet: those are the people your progress is made of.

Growth loves resistance it respects. Put your work in front of one demanding person on a schedule, monthly at least. Ask for the harshest note first. Treat every review on the calendar as training, never as threat.
__ore.retired_v3_definition_friction:
Metal is your Order, and as a friction, it is correction landing harder than you can absorb: every rule met, every critique taken, until standards stop shaping you and start shrinking you.

Diligent, deferential, increasingly small. The inbox of feedback gets read twice, the harsh voice gets memorized, and somewhere along the way the growing itself started asking permission. Rules that were meant to support have become fencing.

Standards should serve the thing growing, never the other way around. Keep the two judges whose notes make you better and mute the rest. Answer critique after a night, never in the hour. Break one harmless rule a month to remember you can.
